transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I guess… I’ve just been feeling really low for the past few weeks. Like there’s this heavy sadness on me most of the day. I can still go to work and smile at patients, but inside I feel like I’m barely keeping it together.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has it been at least two years, or is it more like a few months?
It’s more like weeks… about three weeks, I think. It started not long after I found out I was pregnant.
Has your mood been consistently low every day since this started, or have there been days where you felt somewhat better?
It’s been pretty much every day. I might get through work and look okay, but inside it’s still there… that heavy sadness, most of the day.
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with loved ones?

Yeah… I guess I have. After work I used to paint, or go to yoga, sometimes salsa. Now I mostly just go home and sit on the couch. I don’t really answer texts either. It just feels like… too much effort, I guess.
Have you been feeling fatigued or like you don’t have any energy lately, even if you’ve had enough rest?
I’m not really sure… I mean, I’m tired sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal. It’s hard to tell.
Have you noticed that activities you usually enjoy, like painting or yoga, don’t bring you any pleasure anymore?

Yeah… they don’t really feel like anything right now. I used to paint or go to yoga after my shifts, sometimes salsa, but lately I just go home and sit on the couch. Even answering texts feels like too much.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough, or been blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes, but I haven’t really thought about it that way. I wouldn’t say it’s been a big thing.
Have you been having trouble focusing or thinking clearly lately, like during work or when making decisions?
Yeah… a bit. At work I keep rereading med orders or wound-care notes because it just feels foggy. And decisions I’d normally just make, I kind of freeze and second-guess myself.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still lately?
Yeah… more slowed down, I guess. Everything feels like I’m moving through syrup. Even at the clinic, getting wound supplies together or finishing charting takes me way longer than it should.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating much less or more than usual?

Yeah… I guess I’m eating less. I know I should be eating regular meals, but most days food just doesn’t sound good. Sometimes I’ll be halfway through a clinic shift and realize I’ve only had coffee or some crackers.
Have you lost any significant amount of weight recently, even without trying to?

I haven’t really weighed myself, so I’m not sure. I just know I’m not eating much… like I’ll get halfway through a clinic shift and realize I’ve only had coffee or some crackers. Food just doesn’t really sound good most days.
Have you had any thoughts about death, dying, or hurting yourself lately?
Yeah… I mean, not like I have a plan or anything. But I’ve had thoughts like… I wish I just wouldn’t wake up. That’s what scared me enough to say something at my prenatal appointment.
Have you ever felt this way before, like you’ve had episodes of depression in the past?
I don’t really know… I’ve had rough periods before, I guess, but I’m not sure I’d call it the same.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this one where you felt this level of sadness or loss of interest for a prolonged time?
I’m not sure. I’ve had times where I felt low, but… I don’t know if it was like this, or for this long.
Have you ever had a time in your life before this pregnancy where you felt this low, with a loss of interest in things, for at least two weeks or more?
I honestly don’t know. I’ve had low patches before, but I can’t really say for sure that it was like this for two weeks or more.

inference_history.note: The patient reports feeling low and experiencing heavy sadness for the past few weeks, indicating a possible depressive episode. This opens the differential to include all categories of unipolar depressive disorders, including mild, moderate, severe, and unspecified depressive episodes as well as recurrent depressive disorder and dysthymia.

The duration of symptoms is less than two years and appears to be within a few weeks, making the diagnosis more aligned with a single episode of major depressive disorder rather than recurrent or persistent depressive disorder. The information from this turn rules out F33.x (recurrent depressive disorder) and F34.1 (dysthymia).

The patient has confirmed persistent low mood, anhedonia, and fatigue, which supports the presence of a major depressive episode. Since the duration is less than 2 years, chronic depression (F32.3) is less likely. The distinction between moderate (F32.1) and severe (F32.2 or F32.3) is still unclear, so F32.9 (depression, unspecified) remains as a placeholder. Further clarification on severity and functional impairment is needed.

The patient's symptoms continue to align with major depressive disorder, with no specific features identified to narrow the candidates further. The duration and severity remain consistent with previous candidates.

This turn supports the presence of psychomotor slowing and impaired concentration, which are part of the diagnostic criteria for moderate (F32.2) and severe (F32.3) major depressive episodes. The duration (~3 weeks) and the presence of core and additional symptoms make a diagnosis of major depressive disorder more likely, narrowing the field by ruling out F32.9 (mild depressive episode, which requires fewer symptoms). Further questioning may help distinguish between F32.2 and F32.3.
